identification.summary: Shahid Hemmat is described in press coverage of a State Department Rewards for Justice offer as a hacking group backed by the IRGC Cyber-Electronic Command (IRGC-CEC) [S1]. The same coverage links it to the November 2023 compromise of a booster station at the Municipal Water Authority of Aliquippa, Pennsylvania, and to the CyberAv3ngers name [S1]. In September 2026 the State Department said the IRGC-CEC's Cyber Operations Command head, Amir Yaryab, directs groups including Shahid Hemmat and Shahid Shushtari [S3].
identification.notes: No vendor name or MITRE group ID is established for this record. Secondary reporting ties Shahid Hemmat to the CyberAv3ngers persona [S1], but whether the two are the same entity or one is a cover persona was not confirmed from a primary document. Shahid Shushtari is a separate group in the same reward context [S3].

attribution.sponsor: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Cyber-Electronic Command (IRGC-CEC), per the US State Department Rewards for Justice program as reported by Bitdefender [S1].
attribution.confidence: These are US government allegations relayed by secondary outlets, not adjudicated findings [S1][S3]. The joint advisory AA23-335A attributes the Unitronics PLC activity to IRGC-affiliated actors using the CyberAv3ngers persona, but the search summary did not show it naming Shahid Hemmat [S4].
attribution.basis: State Department Rewards for Justice announcements (October 2024 and 3 September 2026), reported by Bitdefender and Iran International [S1][S3]. Joint advisory AA23-335A on IRGC-affiliated PLC exploitation [S4].

sectors: Energy, news, travel (hotels and airlines), financial and telecommunications (stated for IRGC-CEC groups under Yaryab's direction) [S3]
regions: Europe and the Middle East (stated for groups under Yaryab's direction) [S3]
Israel (CyberAv3ngers claimed attacks since 2020, per Bitdefender) [S1]
targeting.notes: The sector list for the 2026 statement applies to multiple IRGC-CEC groups collectively, not to Shahid Hemmat alone [S3].

capabilities.summary: Reporting describes exploitation of internet-exposed Unitronics Vision Series PLCs, with an attacker message displayed on the device at Aliquippa [S1]. The joint advisory says affiliated IRGC actors compromised internet-facing Unitronics PLCs that used the default password, and that observed activity was defacement with no reported ransomware [S4]. Malware, exploit and infrastructure details specific to Shahid Hemmat are not established in the sources gathered.

campaigns.name: Aliquippa water authority booster station compromise
campaigns.summary: Coverage ties the group to a hack of a booster station at the Municipal Water Authority of Aliquippa, Pennsylvania, which shut down a pump on a line supplying drinking water to nearby towns; the attacker's message appeared on a Unitronics PLC [S1].

campaigns.name: CyberAv3ngers Unitronics PLC exploitation
campaigns.summary: FBI, CISA, NSA, EPA and Israel's INCD reported IRGC-affiliated actors using the CyberAv3ngers persona compromised Unitronics Vision Series PLCs at multiple US water facilities since November 2023 [S4].

campaigns.name: Rewards for Justice offer of up to $10 million
campaigns.summary: The State Department offered up to $10 million for information on four men named as Manuchehr Akbari, Amir Hosein Hoseini, Mohammad Hosein Moradi and Mohammad Reza Rafatinezhad (spellings vary), tied to the IRGC-CEC-backed group accused of attacks on US critical infrastructure including water facilities [S1].

campaigns.name: Reward offer for IRGC-CEC commander Amir Yaryab
campaigns.summary: The State Department offered up to $10 million for information on Yaryab and said he directs groups including Shahid Hemmat and Shahid Shushtari to target US critical infrastructure [S3].

diamond.adversary: IRGC-CEC-backed group; four individuals named in the October 2024 reward offer; Amir Yaryab named as directing commander in September 2026 [S1][S3].
diamond.capability: Exploitation of exposed Unitronics PLCs using default credentials, with defacement-style messages [S1][S4].
diamond.victim: Aliquippa water authority; US water facilities in the broader CyberAv3ngers activity [S1][S4].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing operational technology with default passwords, notably Unitronics Vision Series PLCs in water systems [S4].

gaps: The State Department Rewards for Justice primary notices, CISA AA23-335A full text and Treasury releases could not be opened; WebFetch failed with DNS errors for every host tried, so details rest on search-result summaries of secondary outlets (Bitdefender, SecurityOnline, Iran International, The Record).

Name lists for the reward vary between outlets (one set of names appeared with Lashgarian, Shirinkar and others, which belong to the separate Treasury actions against IRGC-CEC officials); verify against the primary notice.
Relationship between Shahid Hemmat, CyberAv3ngers and Shahid Shushtari (the latter reported with Emennet Pasargad names in a December 2025 offer) is not resolved; do not merge their activity.
No malware families, infrastructure, first-observed date, or objectives are established from the sources gathered.
Whether Treasury sanctions in February 2024 named Shahid Hemmat personnel was not verified.
